deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is not a manuscript but p.17 of the printed offprint of Riemann's 1857 paper 'Beiträge zur Theorie der durch die Gauss'sche Reihe F(α,β,γ,x) darstellbaren Functionen' (Abh. Kgl. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen, Bd. 7, Mathem. Classe). It is the end of Art. V and part of Art. VI. The previous folio carries a dedication and an 'Erbschaft von Justus William Ebell' note. Notation follows Riemann: P(α β γ; α' β' γ'; x) is a P-function with exponents α,α' at 0, β,β' at ∞ and γ,γ' at 1, normalised so that α+α'+β+β'+γ+γ' = 1. P^α, P^{α'}, P^β, ... are its distinguished branches. α_β, α'_β, α_{β'}, ... are the eight quantities from Art. V, ratios of the coefficients expressing the α-branches through the β- and γ-branches; they fix the monodromy.

(1) End of Art. V. The eight monodromy quantities are given as ratios of the form sin((α+β+γ')π)e^{απi} / (sin((α'+β+γ')π)e^{α'πi}), together with the analogous ratios with β' and/or γ in place of β and γ'. Riemann states that they remain unchanged ('ungeändert') when the exponents change by integers.
- Implicit step (mine): shifting α by 1 flips the sign of both sin(α+…)π and e^{απi}, so the numerator is unchanged.
- Shifting β or γ by 1 flips the sign of numerator and denominator alike.
- Hence every ratio is invariant under integer shifts of each exponent separately.

(2) Equal monodromy. Let P and P1 have corresponding exponents differing by integers. Then (α_β)_1 = α_β and so on: one may take all eight quantities equal. Only five of them are arbitrary; the other three follow from the relations among them.

(3) A bilinear combination. As in Art. IV, take W = P^α P1^{α'_1} − P^{α'} P1^{α_1}.
- Rewriting each pair of branches through the β-basis (and γ-basis) gives W = Det(b)(P^β P1^{β'_1} − P^{β'} P1^{β_1}) = Det(c)(P^γ P1^{γ'_1} − P^{γ'} P1^{γ_1}).
- Det(b) and Det(c) are the determinants of the common transition matrices. Because the matrices are the same for P and P1, the same determinant appears.
- W is therefore single-valued: it returns to itself up to a constant factor around each singular point.

(4) W is a polynomial.
- Near 0 the two terms of W behave like x^{α+α'_1} and x^{α'+α_1}. Let ᾱ be the smaller of these two exponents (they differ by an integer). Define β̄ and γ̄ the same way.
- Then F := W·x^{−ᾱ}(1−x)^{−γ̄} is single-valued and finite at x = 0, at x = 1 and at every other finite point.
- At ∞, P^β ~ x^{−β} in Riemann's convention. So W ~ x^{−β̄}, and F grows like x^{−ᾱ−γ̄−β̄}.
- By a Liouville-type argument, F is a polynomial of degree −ᾱ−β̄−γ̄.

(5) Exponent differences. Put λ = α−α', μ = β−β', ν = γ−γ'.
- Then λ+μ+ν = (sum of all exponents) − 2(α'+β'+γ') = 1 − 2(α'+β'+γ').
- Under integer shifts preserving the total sum 1, λ+μ+ν changes by an even integer. Conversely, λ, μ, ν can change by any integers with even sum.
- Define λ1, μ1, ν1 for P1, and Δλ = |λ−λ1|, etc.

(6) Completed on the next page. ᾱ = (α+α'_1+α'+α_1)/2 − Δλ/2, and similarly for β̄ and γ̄. Since the exponents of P and P1 together sum to 2, deg F = (Δλ+Δμ+Δν)/2 − 1. This leads to Art. VII: any three P-functions with integer-differing exponents are linearly related over polynomials, and P satisfies a second-order linear ODE.
errors: No mathematical errors found. 'Ordnung −ᾱ−γ̄−β̄' versus 'Grade −ᾱ−β̄−γ̄' is only a reordering.
The claim that five of the eight quantities determine the other three relies on relations from Art. V and is not reproved here.
The step 'single-valued with polynomial growth implies polynomial' is used tacitly (standard).

results.what: The monodromy invariants (the eight quantities α_β, …) are unchanged under integer shifts of the exponents.
results.modern_name: Monodromy of the Riemann P-equation depends only on exponents mod Z (Riemann–Hilbert data invariance under Schlesinger transformations)

results.what: W·x^{−ᾱ}(1−x)^{−γ̄} is a polynomial of degree (Δλ+Δμ+Δν)/2 − 1, where W is the bilinear combination of two P-functions with integer-shifted exponents.
results.modern_name: Riemann's theorem on contiguous P-functions; generalised Wronskian/Casoratian argument behind Gauss contiguous relations

results.what: λ+μ+ν = 1 − 2(α'+β'+γ') changes by an even integer under integer exponent shifts preserving the sum.
results.modern_name: Parity constraint on exponent-difference shifts (Fuchs relation)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of Riemann's own published 1857 paper on the P-function (Art. V–VI), well known and fully attributed to him.

checkable.asserts: The ratio is invariant under α→α+1 (result 0).

checkable.asserts: The ratio is invariant under β→β+1 (result 0).

transcription_corrections: This is a printed page (p.17 of Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen Bd. 7, Mathem. Classe), not a handwritten manuscript.
The handwritten marginal marks (a bracket and 'b' at the right of the Det line) are not transcribed.
Riemann writes the subscripted quantities as (α_β) with a subscript 1 attached, i.e. (α_β)_1. The transcription's rendering is acceptable.
'die entsprechenden Exponenten α_1 und α': the print shows 'α, und α', i.e. α₁ und α.
Otherwise the transcription matches the image.
